title: Synergia Health - Procurement MSA/DPA/SLAs/Pricing Onboarding
next_steps: Redwood to share MSA + DPA drafts and standard security pack
Redwood SE to schedule benchmark for private deployment (on-prem/VPC) w/ Synergia infra team
Procurement to review pricing sheet and confirm budget approval by 2026-12-22
Legal to return redlines to Redwood by 2026-12-21
action_items: Jordan Lee - Send MSA + DPA drafts and standard security pack - due 2026-12-17
Priya Nambiar - Schedule 2-hour private deployment benchmark and prepare infra checklist - due 2026-12-20
Carlos Vega - Share onboarding checklist and SSO integration notes (SAML) - due 2026-12-18
Mark Doyle (Synergia) - Provide initial legal redlines for MSA/DPA - due 2026-12-21

summary: Redwood AE + SE met with Synergia procurement, legal, security and infra to review MSA/DPA, SLAs, pricing approval path and onboarding timeline. Main customer concerns: data residency, KMS/HSM key control, audit logs, SOC2 scope, and proof of performance for private deployment. Action items: Redwood to send MSA/DPA and security pack, schedule an on-prem/VPC benchmark, and share pricing/commit options for Dedicated vs Hosted. Synergia legal to return redlines within one week.
topics: Pricing and committed capacity vs pay-as-you-go
Security controls: SOC 2, KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan Lee, AE at Redwood. We're joined by Priya our SE and Carlos from CSM. Quick agenda: MSA/DPA, SLAs, pricing approvals and next steps for onboarding.
[00:18] Sara (Synergia - Procurement): Hi all, Sara here. We run procurement for core services, timeline is tight — board wants vendor approvals before year end.
[00:27] Mark (Legal): Mark Doyle, legal counsel. We'll be focused on DPA terms, data residency, and liability caps.
[00:36] Priya (Redwood SE): Great, hi everyone. From the SE side I'll cover deployment options — hosted, dedicated reserved capacity, and private VPC/on-prem options. We'll talk about benchmarks and the security pack.
[00:52] Luis (CTO): Quick note — our primary blocking concern is PII handling and key management. We already use AWS KMS and a HSM for some data. How does Redwood integrate?
[01:05] Priya: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for Private deployments; we have an integration pattern for AWS KMS and can support wrapped keys in on-prem HSMs. For hosted, we offer encrypted-at-rest and envelope encryption but customer-managed KMS is only for Dedicated/Private.
[01:28] Emily (Head of Security): Are audit logs immutable and retained for at least 1 year? We need logs for audits and SOC 2 evidence.
[01:36] Carlos (CSM): We provide audit logs and long-term retention as an add-on. Default retention is 90 days for hosted; dedicated/private offers configurable retention and export to customer S3/ELK.
[01:50] Mark: On the MSA/DPA, we usually ask for specific indemnity language and a 1M liability cap for startups is okay but we'll need to see the insurance certificates. Do you have standard security addendum?
[02:05] Jordan: Yes, we'll share our standard MSA and DPA today. They include our SOC 2 attestation and security pack. We're open to reasonable redlines, but need to understand the specific asks.
[02:18] Sara: Price — we need committed pricing for the first year and clarity on how burst capacity is billed. The finance team wants an expected monthly spend for committed Dedicated vs a host+burst scenario.
[02:31] Priya: For Dedicated we provide reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput; pricing is typically monthly commit. Hosted is pay-as-you-go per token; burst capacity can be configured for both but billing differs. We'll send a pricing matrix with examples and modelled costs based on your estimated workload.
[02:49] Luis: We'll likely test with a 2-week PoC load — 10k requests/day with average 300-token responses. Can you run that on our VPC?
[03:01] Priya: Yes, we can run the benchmark inside your VPC or on-prem. For VPC we'll need firewall rules and a small infra checklist. For on-prem we need machine specs and container runtime info.
[03:15] Anita (Infra Lead): We use k8s (EKS) and have a 4-node GPU cluster as staging. We'll share access details if needed.
[03:23] Priya: Perfect. We'll provide an infra checklist.
[03:30] Mark: Data residency — some of our records must remain in EU. Does Redwood allow region pinning?
[03:38] Jordan: Yes, for Dedicated and Private you can pin regions. Hosted can be region-restricted depending on availability; we'll note EU-hosted options.
[03:46] Emily: About SOC 2, do you scope the model inference layer? We need clarity so our auditors know what is in scope.
[03:54] Carlos: Our SOC 2 report covers the hosted control plane and the Redwood managed components. For Dedicated/Private, customers can opt into shared or separate scopes; we'll provide a map of responsibilities (RACI) in the security pack.
[04:08] Sara: What's the SLA on latency and uptime? For clinical use cases we need 99.9% uptime and p99 latency below 300ms for short prompts.
[04:20] Priya: We offer SLA tiers; 99.9% uptime is standard for Dedicated with SLA credits. P99 latency is workload-dependent; we publish model performance profiles. For low-latency SLAs we recommend specific model/quantization combos and Dedicated capacity.
[04:40] Luis: How do you handle fallback in case the dedicated pool is saturated? We can't have app-facing errors.
[04:48] Jordan: We support smart routing and automated fallback to compatible model variants or hosted capacity. That said, fallbacks may change latency and cost; we'll document behavior in the runbook.
[05:02] Mark: Regarding the DPA — can we get a clause for deletion upon contract termination and a 30-day data return window?
[05:10] Jordan: Yes, standard is data deletion and export within 30 days; we can add explicit export formats in the DPA.
[05:20] Priya: Also worth noting, for Private we can keep all KV cache and prefixes within your VPC, which reduces egress and keeps PII internal.
[05:34] Anita: For the bench, do you need us to seed real-ish data? We prefer synthetic but representative datasets.
[05:42] Priya: Synthetic representative datasets are perfect — avoids PHI exposure. We'll send a test harness and script.
[05:52] Sara: On procurement timeline — we have a vendor approval meeting on 2026-12-22, so we need price and initial contract terms before then.
[06:02] Jordan: Understood. We'll prioritize pricing and MSA/DPA drafts today.
[06:10] Mark: A couple of quick redline asks: narrower subprocessing list, more specific breach notification timelines (48 hours), and clarifying indemnity for data breaches.
[06:23] Jordan: We'll flag those for legal. We usually do 72 hours for incident notification but open to 48 for enterprise. We'll escalate to legal for the indemnity wording.
[06:37] Emily: Do you support SSO with SAML and SCIM for user provisioning?
[06:44] Carlos: Yes, SAML SSO is supported plus SCIM for user sync on the Console. We'll share docs.
[06:52] Luis: For private infra, what's the expected lead time to onboard?
[06:58] Priya: Typically 3-6 weeks for Private (depending on on-prem vs VPC), 1-2 weeks for Dedicated if capacity is available.
[07:10] Anita: Any licensing differences for model families/quantized variants? We have internal rules about LLM licensing.
[07:16] Priya: We can map which models are available under our hosting and what licensing constraints exist. For some open models we can provide local deployment variants.
[07:28] Jordan: I'll add model licensing notes to the pack.
[07:34] Mark: Do you have cyber insurance? We need to see certs and limits.
[07:38] Jordan: Yes, we'll include insurance certificate with MSA.
[07:44] Sara: Pricing — can you give a ballpark for a Dedicated 3-month demo? We want a committed minimal pool to run the PoC.
[07:53] Priya: For a small Dedicated pool supporting your 10k req/day, rough estimate is $Xk/month for reserved GPUs plus usage for burst. We'll send a numeric matrix in the pricing sheet.
[08:05] Emily: Are there any penetration test reports or third-party attestation we can see?
[08:11] Carlos: We have penetration test summaries and third-party pen tests; full reports are available under NDA. We'll attach summaries first.
[08:22] Jordan: Ok, to recap: Redwood will send MSA/DPA, security pack, pricing matrix, infra checklist and schedule the benchmark with Priya. Synergia legal/procurement will return redlines by 2026-12-21/22.
[08:38] Mark: Sounds good. Also curious about support SLAs and escalation matrix.
[08:44] Carlos: We'll include a support SLA and escalation contact list in the pack. For enterprise customers we can provide 24x7 on-call options.
[08:55] Sara: If possible please include a sample PO template for finance.
[09:00] Jordan: We'll include a sample PO and contract signature instructions.
[09:08] Priya: For the bench we'll need access to a staging cluster; I'll follow up with Anita and Luis to schedule next week.
[09:20] Anita: I'll provision environment details by EOD tomorrow.
[09:26] Jordan: Great. Any other questions?
[09:30] Luis: One small thing on logging — are logs writable to our SIEM in near real-time?
[09:36] Priya: Yes, we can stream logs to customer S3 or a push to your SIEM via secure transport; latency is typically under a minute for log forwarding.
[09:46] Emily: On encryption in transit — TLS 1.3?
[09:49] Carlos: TLS 1.3 is standard end-to-end.
[09:54] Mark: Ok that's all for me.
[09:58] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs. Expect emails today.
[10:05] Sara: Thanks, talk soon.
[52:00] (call ends)
